- When sentiment is consistently negative (avg < -0.2) over recent days, model tends to overcorrect upward — reduce forecast peak by 5–10%.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > +10% above recent mean), model often overshoots — cap next 3–5 days’ forecast at +5% above peak.
- If sentiment is positive but price is trending down, model underreacts — add 2–3% upward bias to forecast for next 5 days.
- Model frequently overestimates mean reversion in short-term (1–3 days) — adjust downward by 1–3% if sentiment is neutral or slightly negative.
- When sentiment is volatile (±0.3 or more), model tends to lag — forecast 1–2 days ahead of true price, especially if sentiment is trending upward.
- If sentiment is negative and price is rising, model often misreads momentum — reduce forecast slope by 10–20% for next 3 days.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to overestimate volatility — cap forecast range within ±10% of recent 14-day moving average.
